e: Dengue commonly causes thrombocytopenia and bleeding manifestations; fever with petechiae strongly supports dengue.
Trichomonas vaginalis is a motile flagellated protozoan; characteristic darting/twitching motility is seen on a fresh wet mount.
Leishmania amastigotes contain a nucleus and kinetoplast and are found intracellularly in macrophages; cutaneous leishmaniasis occurs in Rajasthan.
Cytomegalovirus produces characteristic intranuclear inclusion bodies with an 'owl's-eye' appearance.
Chronic Clonorchis sinensis infection causes biliary inflammation and epithelial changes and increases the risk of cholangiocarcinoma.
Pneumocystis jirovecii causes pneumonia in advanced HIV infection; its cysts are characteristically demonstrated by Gomori methenamine silver staining.

Leptospirosis causes fever, conjunctival suffusion, jaundice and renal involvement after exposure to contaminated water or animal urine; the microscopic agglutination test is the standard serological test.
Rotavirus diarrhea can be diagnosed by detecting viral antigen in stool, commonly by enzyme immunoassay or rapid antigen testing.
HRP-2 is a Plasmodium falciparum-specific antigen used in rapid diagnostic tests.
Haemophilus influenzae is a pleomorphic gram-negative coccobacillus requiring X and V factors; it shows satellitism around Staphylococcus aureus on blood agar.
Intracellular gram-negative diplococci in urethral discharge indicate Neisseria gonorrhoeae; ceftriaxone is the recommended treatment for uncomplicated gonococcal infection.
CSF PCR for HSV DNA is the preferred confirmatory test for HSV encephalitis.
After a positive filarial antigen test, examination of a properly timed peripheral blood smear can demonstrate microfilariae and help identify the infecting parasite.
Measles virus (paramyxovirus): single-stranded (negative-sense) enveloped RNA virus; Koplik spots + rash starting behind the ears

W. bancrofti microfilariae: sheathed, nuclei do not extend to the tail tip.
Brugia malayi: 2 terminal nuclei at the tail tip

Cream pastry/custard → Staph. aureus preformed enterotoxin → vomiting within 1–6 h.
B. cereus → fried rice
Pseudomonas aeruginosa: slender gram-negative bacilli (pink rods), oxidase +ve, pyocyanin pigment
Painless chancre = syphilis; Treponema pallidum is too thin for light microscopy → dark-field microscopy shows its motility
Swabs/soiled dressings go into the yellow bag (incineration)

Strep. pneumoniae is the commonest cause of lobar pneumonia, even in HIV.
Pneumocystis → diffuse bilateral interstitial infiltrates
Prozone: antibody excess prevents lattice formation → false negative; dilution restores the optimal ratio → positive
Strongyloides hyperinfection in steroid-treated patients (autoinfection); larvae in BAL; larva currens → urticaria
Blood spills are disinfected c̅ 1% sodium hypochlorite (bleach)

Selenite F = enrichment broth for enteric pathogens (Salmonella, Shigella) from stool.
Alkaline peptone water = Vibrio cholerae
Leishmania (amastigote/promastigote) has a kinetoplast; vector = sandfly (Phlebotomus)
GAS adheres to pharyngeal epithelium via lipoteichoic acid (c̅ M protein, protein F) binding fibronectin
Weil's disease (Leptospirosis): fever, jaundice, renal failure, conjunctival suffusion after sewage/rat urine exposure
Campylobacter jejuni: curved ('seagull') gram-negative rods; raw milk/poultry; bloody diarrhea; GBS association
Enterobius egg: D-shaped (planoconvex) c̅ thin shell & larva; picked up by cellophane (Scotch) tape
Histoplasma: tuberculate macroconidia in culture; tissue form = small narrow-based budding yeast inside macrophages
Nocardia: gram-positive branching filaments, weakly acid-fast (modified ZN); paraffin bait culture; brain abscess/meningitis

Aspergillus: septate hyphae c̅ acute-angle (45°) dichotomous branching.
Mucor: aseptate, ribbon-like, wide-angle branching
HSV: Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells c̅ intranuclear (Cowdry A) inclusions
Recurrent Neisseria infections → terminal complement (C5–C9, MAC) deficiency
B. anthracis: capsulated bacilli (bamboo-stick); McFadyean reaction = purple capsule c̅ polychrome methylene blue; malignant pustule
Microfilaria on smear = filariasis → lymphatic obstruction (lymphedema/elephantiasis)
